events.text: You climb the old pear tree behind the house to see over the wall, and come down with a long tear in {outfit}. Someone is going to notice.

choices.text: Mend the tear yourself before anyone sees

effects.log: Your stitches wander like a lost goose, but the tear is shut, and you learn how a needle thinks.

choices.text: Tell the truth at supper

effects.log: There is a scolding, and then, when nobody is looking, a pear left on your pillow.

events.text: After the spring rain the lane is one long puddle. The other children dare you to cross it on the stepping stones without a single splash on {outfit}.

choices.text: Cross it, light as a sparrow

effects.log: Stone, stone, stone, and you are over, dry to the ankles. The other children stare at you for a whole day.

choices.text: Walk straight through it

effects.log: You wade through the middle and come out brown to the knees, laughing. Somebody has to be the brave one.

events.text: At dawn you go down to the still pond where nobody comes, brush the dust from {outfit}, and practise with {weapon_look} until your reflection stops looking like someone pretending.

choices.text: Practise until the sun is high

effects.log: By noon the draw is clean and quiet. The reflection in the pond looks like someone you could become.

choices.text: Sit and watch the water instead

effects.log: A carp rises, takes a fly and is gone. You think about that for the rest of the day.

events.text: A group of young disciples from a richer house laugh at {outfit} in the market square, loudly enough to be sure you hear it.

choices.text: Smile and keep walking

effects.log: You keep walking. By the next street you have forgotten their faces; they will not forget that you did.

choices.text: Turn and look at them until they stop

effects.log: You turn and look, and say nothing at all. One by one they find something interesting in a fruit stall.

events.text: A travelling tailor with a mouthful of pins stops you on the road, walks once around you and says {outfit} is the best-worn thing in three counties. The hem, though. The hem is a crime.

choices.text: Let the tailor fix the hem (10 taels)

effects.log: Ten taels and one cup of tea later the hem hangs true, and you walk a little straighter for it.

choices.text: Thank the tailor and walk on

effects.log: You bow, and the tailor sighs at your hem all the way to the next village.

events.text: A cold rain catches you on an open road, miles from any roof. {outfit} is soaked through in a moment, and you wrap {weapon_look} in oilcloth under your arm.

choices.text: Shelter under the eaves of a roadside shrine

effects.log: The shrine has a broken roof and a dry corner. You sleep there with the rain on the tiles and wake warm.

choices.text: Walk on through it

effects.log: You walk through the rain until it gives up. Your boots squelch for two days; your legs remember it longer.

events.text: A street painter at the bridge asks to paint you, just as you stand: {outfit}, {weapon_look}, the river behind. "People buy faces like yours," the painter says, "to hang over a door."

choices.text: Sit for the portrait (15 taels)

effects.log: The painting is not quite you and not quite not. A month later you see a copy of it over a teahouse door.

choices.text: Say you are only passing through

effects.log: The painter shrugs and sketches you anyway, three strokes, from behind, walking away.

events.text: In a village by the river the children have made copies of {outfit} out of sacking, and a stick each for {weapon_look}, and are fighting each other as you, very badly, in the lane.

choices.text: Show them a real stance

effects.log: You show them one stance, properly. For years after, every child in that village stands exactly like you.

choices.text: Pretend you have not seen

effects.log: You walk past with a straight face. Behind you, someone falls over, and is declared the winner.

events.text: At a crowded inn a stranger looks up, takes in {outfit} and {weapon_look}, and knows you before you have said a word. The whole table goes quiet.

choices.text: Raise your cup to the table

effects.log: You raise your cup. The table raises theirs. By morning the story of it has grown in the telling.

choices.text: Pay for your rice and leave quietly

effects.log: You leave before the talk can start. On the road you think about how a look can walk ahead of you.

events.text: In the crush of a festival market a small hand tugs at {weapon_look}. You look down at a thin child who has clearly never tried this on anyone in {outfit} before, and is starting to regret it.

choices.text: Catch the wrist, gently

effects.log: You catch the wrist, buy the child a bun with your free hand, and let go. The child runs; the bun goes too.

choices.text: Let the child run

effects.log: You let go and watch the child vanish into the crowd. Whatever they needed, it was more than you did.

events.text: Washing at the basin one morning you catch yourself in the water: {outfit} gone soft with years, {weapon_look} hanging by the door where it always hangs. You stay looking longer than you mean to.

choices.text: Remember the first time you wore it

effects.log: You remember the first morning, and the person you were. You would like to tell them it was worth it.

choices.text: Splash the face and get on with the day

effects.log: Cold water, a deep breath, and the day. There is still a great deal of it left.

events.text: A young visitor at your gate asks, a little shyly, whether {outfit} was always the fashion, or whether you made it one.

choices.text: Tell the long story

effects.log: You tell the long story, and leave out the boring parts, and add a few that never happened at all.

choices.text: Laugh and say you never noticed

effects.log: You laugh. The visitor goes away certain that you invented it, and tells everyone so.
